title: Relative flatness and a flat fibre stalk give a free neighbourhood
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, and $\mathcal F_s$ be its tensor pullback to the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] and $(\mathcal F_s)_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then there are an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X$ of $x$ and an integer $r\geq0$ with $\mathcal F|_W\cong\mathcal O_W^{\oplus r}$.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-finite-presentation-stalk-fibre-data at x. Write R=O_{S,f(x)}, B=O_{X,x}, M=F_x. Its finite free presentation gives Module.FinitePresentation B M: the kernel of the displayed surjection is the range of its finite free relation map, hence finitely generated. Retain the essentially finitely presented local algebra model P, its localization T, and the compatible fibre quotient equivalences theta and eta.

Split on whether M is subsingleton. In that case M is free, with the empty basis, directly. Otherwise M is nontrivial. Restrict scalars through the actual local stalk map R to B; relative flatness is Module.Flat R M. Through theta and eta, lem-pc-flat-semilinear-equiv transfers fibre stalk flatness to flatness of M/(m_R B)M over B/m_R B. The quotient-tensor equivalence identifies this quotient with (B/m_R B) tensor_B M, linearly over the quotient ring. Apply lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre to R to B to B, the second map the identity, and the same presentation P,T twice. The conclusion makes M flat over B, and lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free makes M free.

In either case the finite free B-module M has the basis Module.finBasis indexed by Fin r, with r its finite rank. Apply lem-trf-finite-presentation-stalk-basis-spread to X.toRingedSpace, F and that basis; invert its isomorphism. Scheme.Modules.overIsoFreeEquiv converts the over-site trivialization to the scheme restriction, and restrictFreeIso identifies the restriction of the free module on X with the free module on W. Compose to obtain exactly the required isomorphism. This also handles rank zero.
